GOTCHA (2026-06-27, colleague v1.27.0, commit 4f9a26b): agentfront 0.15.0 added Flag(choices=) (issue #38 Ask 1), but it does NOT enable parse-time choices on a VALUE-CARRYING flag in a rendered tool — a flag whose value the function consumes via its signature param. agentfront derives a CLI arg from EACH signature param and its dispatcher forwards ONLY signature params. Empirically vs installed 0.15.0: Shape A (sig param `algo` + explicit Flag([--algo],choices=)) COLLIDES at build (argparse `conflicting option string: --algo`; agentfront sets no conflict_handler=resolve). Shape B (Flag-only --algo, NOT in signature — agentfront own test shape in test_cli_surface._checksum_app) validates the choice but SILENTLY DROPS the value (dispatcher never forwards a non-signature arg). add_command is top-level-only, so converting the noun to a host command (which would get native argparse choices) would EVICT the whole noun from the MCP/learn catalog — wrong trade. RESOLUTION in colleague: validate --algo EXPLICITLY + EARLY inside the verb (commands/hooks approve) — a clean choices-shaped CliError against the new public colleague.policy.SUPPORTED_CHECKSUM_ALGOS tuple, raised before any file/name lookup. A fully general fix would be a further agentfront ask: let an explicit Flag REPLACE a signature-derived arg of the same dest (suppress sig-derivation when an explicit Flag covers it). Public run_tool accessor (Ask 2) WAS cleanly adoptable: app.mcp_server().run_tool replaces the private _build_run_tool in tests.

Dual-model deepthink design decision (spec/dual-model-deepthink, 2026-07-01): forced synthesis (#191) and fill-line compaction (#156) STAY on the MAIN model even in dual-model config. Reason: their prompt IS the main model's own windowed history (up to Gemma's ~128K budget), which structurally cannot fit the deepthink model's 64K window - re-windowing to fit would discard half the context and degrade the result. Deepthink (Qwen) is reachable only where the prompt is naturally digest-sized: the backend-judged deepthink loop tool, plan-mode proposals, the acceptance self-check, and the test-integrity reviewer default. Review verdicts escalate via the TOOL (main model composes a 64K-fitting digest); review-mode-driving-WITH-Qwen is a parked mode-level-preference follow-up. Also: the devague convergence gate requires honesty conditions on the narrative claims (announcement/audience/after/before/why) and the boundary claim, not just requirement kinds.

lobes gotcha (probed live 2026-07-03, gateway http://localhost:8001): in the /capabilities payload, each role's own `endpoint` field is NOT client-reachable (reports an internal :8000 that 404s on /v1/* and /capabilities). Consumers must dial the GATEWAY ORIGIN (the URL that served /capabilities, e.g. :8001) which routes by model-id, treating the per-role `endpoint`/`path` fields as informational only. colleague's cortex/senses arc works around this (config._lobes_base_url derives base_url from the gateway origin). Filed upstream as lobes-cli#87.

colleague hot-file gotcha: EngineConfig.resolve and cli/_commands/session.py _Session.__init__ were already AT SonarCloud's S107 13-parameter limit, so adding ANY new param (e.g. discover_lobes, cortex_only/debug_senses) trips S107 on the PR. Fix pattern that worked (PR #281): bundle rarely-used/env-only knobs into a frozen options dataclass — ResolveOverrides (8 env-only knobs off resolve()), SessionIO(out,err) + SensesSessionOptions(cortex_only,debug_senses). Before bundling, grep every `.resolve(`/constructor call-site (prod + tests) to confirm no PROD caller passes the bundled params — only then is it byte-identical. Tracked as the broader hot-file refactor #280.

Proof-design lesson (from colleague cortex-senses livecheck, PR #281 review): a live proof/livecheck must never supply the very evidence it verifies. The cortex-senses check initially did `if result.senses is None: result.senses = SensesBlock(mode=split, packet=packet)` — fabricating the block from the session-side packet — so it would PASS even if the loop regressed and recorded nothing. Fix: grade the artifact the code ACTUALLY produced; if the loop recorded no block, let classify FAIL it. Also: a GRACEFUL degrade on a genuinely-serving rig (e.g. senses intake returns malformed JSON → packet None) must SKIP, not FAIL — degrade-to-raw is correct behavior, not a regression.

colleague oilcheck invariant: a registered doctor check-group is contractually NO-NETWORK (only the opt-in --probe reachability group may dial out). A new config-resolution rung that makes a network call when armed (the lobes rung: EngineConfig.resolve → resolve_roles GET) leaks a network call + stderr notice into a plain `colleague doctor`, because the provider group calls resolve(). Fix (PR #281): give resolve() a `discover_lobes: bool = True` param (default byte-identical); the offline provider group passes discover_lobes=False; the live lobes check lives only in the --probe reachability group. Add a regression test that the provider group never calls resolve_roles when armed.

SonarCloud python:S7632 ("Fix the syntax of this issue suppression comment.", MAJOR) flags the repo common `# noqa: CODE - inline prose` form as malformed suppression syntax — e.g. `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a best-effort informational extra`. flake8 tolerates the trailing prose (it stops parsing codes at the first non-code token) but Sonar stricter rule does not. FIX: use canonical `# noqa: BLE001` and relocate the reason to a preceding comment line at the same indent as `except`. GOTCHA: S7632 is a newer rule and Sonar PR analysis only reports issues on CHANGED lines, so the repo ~15 pre-existing `# noqa: CODE - reason` lines (organs.py:267, voice.py:123, tools.py:778) are NOT flagged until touched — only newly-added/changed ones trip it. Seen on PR #298 (colleague#291), organs.py:429, fixed commit 0044243. Note `# nosec B310 - prose` (bandit, no colon) is different syntax and is NOT flagged by S7632.
